definition: Dated company-reported capture evidence for the core research queue. Each record preserves reported facts, the project interpretation, and a counterpoint. These are not agent-specific revenue disclosures unless the company explicitly says so.

facts: Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue: $99M, +39% year over year
CIS contract commitments: more than $2.8B year to date, including a greater-than-$600M robotics contract
Non-GAAP operating margin: 25%, down five points year over year
records.captureRead: Early capture evidence. CIS growth and commitments support an AI-infrastructure hypothesis, but no agent-specific revenue, pricing, or attach rate is disclosed.
records.counterpoint: Delivery and other cloud-applications revenue declined, while future cloud and AI capacity is expected to increase capital and operating costs.

records.sourceLabel: Elastic Q1 FY2027 results and Form 10-Q
facts: Elastic Cloud revenue: $235M, +20% year over year, 49% of revenue
Sales-led subscription revenue: $399M, +18% year over year
Total gross margin: 74%, down from 77% year over year
records.captureRead: Mechanism and consumption exposure are visible, but agent-specific usage, pricing, retention, and cash-flow proof are not disclosed.
records.counterpoint: Cloud-hosting costs rose faster than subscription revenue and pressured gross margin.

records.sourceLabel: Dynatrace Q1 FY2027 results and Form 10-Q
facts: Annualized logs consumption: $200M, growing more than 100% year over year
Subscription gross margin: 85%, down from 86% year over year
records.captureRead: Usage and product relevance are visible, but no agent-specific ARR, revenue, pricing, or retention cohort is disclosed.
records.counterpoint: Higher cloud-hosting costs and expected acquisition-related margin dilution remain material tests.

records.sourceLabel: F5 Q3 FY2026 results and Form 10-Q
records.captureRead: AI Gateway makes the company product-relevant, but adoption, attach, customer count, pricing, and revenue are not disclosed.
records.counterpoint: Growth was led by systems, and the gateway could remain a bundled feature rather than a paid control-plane product.
